management_steps.details: Bradycardia: indicates CCB, BB, Digoxin, Clonidine, or lithium. Tachycardia: indicates anticholinergics, antihistamines, sympathomimetics (cocaine, amphetamines). AF: alcohol binge (holiday heart) or withdrawal. Ventricular Fibrillation: verapamil in AF+WPW.

PR Prolongation (>200ms): BB, CCB, Digoxin, TCA. QRS Prolongation (>100ms): Sodium channel blockade (TCA, carbamazepine, local anaesthetics, cocaine). QTc Prolongation: Potassium channel blockade (TCA, sotalol, antihistamines). J Wave: hypothermia. Scooped ST segment (Salvador Dali moustache): Digoxin.
Right Axis Deviation (terminal R wave > 3mm in aVR, or R/S ratio > 0.7 in aVR) indicates fast sodium channel blockade (highly predictive of TCA seizures/arrhythmias).
